analysis:
Examined docs/architecture/inference.md:420–1216, covering Super admission and shared-memory accounting, authenticated prefix-cache scope, encrypted durable checkpoints and artifact/prompt bindings, logprobs, cancellation/billing, media limits, and native retirement; also GLM artifact verification, ownership receipts, paged execution and capacity refusal. These intersect A-001, A-003, A-004, A-018, T-007, T-010, T-027, T-028, T-041 and T-050. The complete range map places this file's changes at head:3541–3575, outside both supplied source excerpts; therefore the surrounding cache and inference descriptions do not establish a new regression. In particular, differences between these existing descriptions and T-041's RAM-tier posture should not be attributed to this PR.
The bounded patch introduces documentation of cluster listener rebinding and pairing refresh, including retaining a listener when the pairing store is unreadable. This is orientation evidence, not enough to establish a vulnerability. Integration should examine the changed listener behavior in provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Distributed/Onboarding/ClusterService.swift and related pairing/control code: how responder and lease authorization change on re-pairing, removal or cable changes, whether stale control authority is withdrawn, and the security contract during pairing-store read failures. No runtime implementation or exact changed numbered source for that behavior is supplied here, so its trust-boundary impact remains unresolved rather than cleared.
